business_problem: Matawan needed to move beyond rigid server and VM infrastructure that required heavy manual operations, because its mobility SaaS platform had to absorb traffic peaks, stay continuously available, and support international growth without ballooning operating costs.
solution_summary: Matawan migrated its mobility platform toward Google Cloud in stages so transit operators could keep running without interruption while the architecture shifted from tightly coupled virtual machines to modular managed services. Google Kubernetes Engine became the primary orchestration layer for containerized independent services, Cloud Run handles highly variable processes with serverless elasticity, and Compute Engine provides the remaining core compute foundation during the transition. On the data side, Cloud SQL supports critical transactional databases, Cloud Storage handles large-scale storage, and BigQuery gives operators near-real-time analytical visibility into transit usage patterns. This architecture helps Matawan process ticket validations, payments, passenger information, and mobility data with better resilience and less operational toil. It also supports international expansion, faster service launches, and AI-enabled mobility innovation with Gemini.

data_flow: Transit validations, payments, passenger information, and mobility data flow through GKE-hosted and Cloud Run services, persist in transactional and storage systems, and are analyzed in BigQuery so operators can see network patterns while Matawan keeps scaling new mobility services.
business_outcome: Matawan now processes over 150 million transit-pass validations a year, handles nearly five times more validations at equivalent infrastructure cost, cut CO2 emissions by 43%, and launches new services faster with much less operational effort.
